The test image shows a tomato leaf with multiple dark brown/black spots scattered across the surface. Spots are round to irregular, moderate in size, no obvious yellow halos. Top candidates: Septoria Leaf Blotch, Early Blight, Bacterial Speck, Alternaria Black Molds.

Now I'll view one reference from each of 8 different classes.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Green tomato leaf (appears to be underside), scattered dark brown/black spots, round to irregular, moderate size, no clear yellow halos, leaf still predominantly green.
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** (CDDM_1928): Very similar - scattered dark spots on green tomato leaves, same overall pattern.
- **Bacterial_Speck** (Bugwood_14): Similar dark spots but with visible yellow halos not seen in test image.
- **Early_Blight** (CDDM_1107): Botanical illustration, larger target-board spots, different pattern.
- **Alternaria** (Bugwood_13): Microscopic spore view, not comparable.
- **Late_Blight** (PlantVillage_195): Extensive brown necrosis, very different.
- **TSWV** (Bugwood_3): Whole-plant wilting, no leaf spots.
- **Gray_Mold** (Bugwood_13): Fruit rot, not leaf spots.
- **Septoria** (CDDM_2685): More advanced stage with merging dark spots - same disease, different severity.

The test image most closely matches Septoria Leaf Blotch — multiple scattered dark spots on green leaf tissue, consistent with early-to-mid stage Septoria lycopersici infection.
